docChanges.newValue: Building and Research Duration Units and Day Components
Verified TimeSpan configuration parsing, effective duration estimates, day-aware UI and migration of legacy queued building durations.

# Building and Research duration units

## Root cause and verified source — 2026-11-13

`scripts/generate-building-data.mjs` previously split a duration by `:` and converted the first component directly to a number of hours. Server durations use the .NET TimeSpan shape `[days.]hours:minutes:seconds`, so `4.10:59:00` became4.1hours+59minutes=18,300seconds instead of385,140seconds. This affected102of3,294building-level rows, starting where day components appear. It was a metadata-generation error, not a JavaScript integer-overflow or clock-formatting limit.

| Configuration | Verified MD5 / immutable source |
| --- | --- |
| Building levels | `8f8820e1d76bbfa899e8bdf9241880bf` — `https://hwmb-remote-config-cdn.nextersglobal.com/config/buildingLevel/8f8820e1d76bbfa899e8bdf9241880bf.json` |
| Current research levels | `b587adca0646f9a24abf202da822c321` — `https://hwmb-remote-config-cdn.nextersglobal.com/config/personalResearchLevel/b587adca0646f9a24abf202da822c321.json` |

Both hashes match the captured `indexGet.index.configs` map in `temp/remote-config-captured.json`. Building bytes were checked directly; the research source was fetched from the pinned current URL and MD5-verified. All898current research durations already matched generated metadata, including day components. No research table values needed changing. Older `temp/personalResearchLevel.json` has a different hash; do not treat that older file as the current config without verification.

Hall of Heroes (building20), target level21:

- Raw `4.10:59:00` =4days10hours59minutes =385,140seconds.
- Existing building estimate multiplier0.58 gives223,381,200milliseconds, approximately2days14hours3minutes1.2seconds.
- The old parsed18,300seconds gave10,614,000milliseconds, explaining the reported2h56m display.

Other verified research examples: research568level5=`07.19:30:00`=675,000seconds; research634level1=`01.09:40:00`=121,200seconds; research635level1=`02.14:30:00`=225,000seconds.

## Parsing and units

`parseRemoteDurationSeconds` in `scripts/lib/remote-duration.mjs` handles optional days, zero-padded day/hour fields, ordinary hour durations, legacy minute:second strings and non-negative integer seconds. Malformed formats, invalid minute/second fields, out-of-range hours with an explicit day component, and unsafe integers fail rather than silently truncating.

The generator verifies source MD5 against the captured index before writing `extension/building-data.js`. Metadata `d` is always base seconds. `calculateEffectiveDurationMs` converts seconds to milliseconds once, then applies the existing speed multiplier. The default estimates remain0.58for Building and0.892for Research; this fix does not establish those as universal account-specific speed bonuses. Explicit caller multipliers remain supported. Live server queue timestamps/durations remain authoritative.

`getQueueEnd`, timelines, planned `startConstruction`/`startResearch` arguments and wake deadlines use full millisecond values; a multi-day duration must never be treated as a time of day or truncated with a clock-only parser.

## Saved automation queue migration

The generated building helper retains the exact historical bad seconds only for the102affected rows. `normalizeQueuedDuration` repairs an automation item's duration only when its building/target level is affected and its saved milliseconds exactly match the old default0.58estimate. It preserves identities and other fields and leaves unrelated/custom estimates unchanged.

`normalizeQueuedItem` applies this correction in Building timeline and planning helpers. `runCityQueue` also persists repaired automation items and emits a `repair` log before future dispatch. Disabled queues can display the repaired timeline and are persisted when evaluation resumes. Repeated normalization is idempotent.

Do not rewrite already-issued `pendingRequest.calls`/`startedItem`, server `buildingStatus`/`researchStatus` queue durations, active start/end times, or historical upgrade records. Pending requests still require normal authoritative acknowledgement/reconciliation. The migration updates future estimates, not a running server operation.

## UI

`formatDuration` displays days, remaining hours and minutes for durations of24hours or longer; sub-day formatting stays compatible. `formatFinishTime` includes month/day for another local date and year when it differs, preventing a multi-day completion from looking like a same-day clock time. Building and Research dialogs use it for active, queued, total and candidate finish estimates. Execution-log timestamps remain clock times.

## Regeneration and verification

1. Obtain a current complete `indexGet` and its exact `buildingLevel` bytes. Save them at the paths consumed by `scripts/generate-building-data.mjs`; hashes must match.
2. Run `npm run building:metadata`. Do not manually edit the generated table. Use the same TimeSpan parser for future research metadata generation/audits.
3. Compare every source row's parsed duration to generated `d`; ensure non-duration fields remain unchanged when fixing only duration parsing. On2026-11-13 this verified all3,294building rows and all898current research durations. All102legacy default estimates were checked against their corrected values.
4. Run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and the versioned production build.

`tests/city-duration.test.mjs` covers the parser, Hall example, multi-day Research values, exact migration and exclusions, timelines, RPC payloads, wait deadlines, authoritative server durations and formatting boundaries. `tests/city-queue-ui.test.mjs` evaluates the actual Building dialog candidate/timeline computeds. `tests/background.test.mjs` checks persisted migration and unchanged in-flight payloads.

Implemented by @task-VHE-R07HP4. Related: @doc/architecture/building-and-research-queue-reconciliation.
